title: Guide a first-time user from requirement to one safe delivery
acceptance: A first-time Codex user can describe an outcome naturally and is guided through outcome, acceptance criteria, non-goals, delivery target, and one fresh autonomy choice without knowing plugin IDs or JSON.
The public sequence is requirement agreement, decomposition when needed, output and work brief agreement, one delivery profile, one task start, implementation, verification, and delivery.
Fresh init and status hide untouched bootstrap contracts and show the single meaningful next action for onboarding or the first requirement.
Requirement intake and decomposition are not blocked by a contract that can only be created later, and approval requests include only the active story or phase.
CLI help documents every runtime-required input and clearly distinguishes the conversational Codex front door from deterministic structured CLI recovery.
Starter prompts and a plain-language guide cover assessment, a new PR, an existing PR, and local-only work, while explaining local execution, repository publication, and deployment separately.
Existing tests, new novice black-box journeys, check, doctor, package validation, strict story gate, remote CI, and a post-merge main verification all pass.
